messages:
maya: Heads-up — CI microbench on PR #9387 failed the batcher/kv throughput golden. batcher_kv_throughput dropped ~12% vs baseline (12000 -> 10560). Threshold is -5%, so this is a hard fail.
cheng: CI job: https://ci.redwood/internal/124567 — logs show attn_kernel time increased and a big KV hitrate drop.
tariq: quick skim — PR #9387 changed kernel_autoselect scoring and also switched KV key normalization to drop session ids. Both are potential suspects.
eli: perf summary from the failing run:
```
Benchmark: batcher_kv_throughput
Baseline mean: 12000.2 ops/s
PR mean: 10560.8 ops/s
Diff: -12.0% (threshold -5%)
p-value: 0.0004
Top op time delta: attn_kernel  +18ms per batch
KV hitrate: baseline 72% -> PR 56%
```
sam: a 16% relative drop in KV hitrate is massive — that alone could explain the perf. Any code that touches key generation/serialization in this PR?
maya: yes — PR normalized inputs before hashing to canonicalize tokens, removed trailing session suffix. My note: normalization code trims whitespace with `.strip()` which likely removes more than intended for short sequences.
cheng: repro locally with the small script: `python perf/repro_kv_hitrate.py --seed 42 --seq-len 64` shows hitrate collapse when the normalization branch is enabled.
tariq: I did a quick bisect on the PR branch — if I revert the normalization commit (commit 7f3b9d), throughput recovers to ~11950 ops/s. If I disable the kernel_autoselect scoring tweak but keep the normalization change, perf still bad. So normalization is the larger culprit.
maya: plan: open a revert for the normalization change immediately, keep kernel_autoselect as a feature-flagged experiment while we add unit tests for key stability. I'll open the revert PR.
ci-bot: Revert PR created: https://ci.redwood/pull/9391 — restores previous KV key generation. CI and microbench jobs triggered.
eli: can someone run the microbench with env `KV_CACHE=1` and the same seed to validate?
tariq: kicked off the bench for PR 9391, ETA ~20m.
sam: thanks — if that restores hitrate, we can unblock the rollout and then rework normalization with explicit tests. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Bench result for PR 9391: batcher_kv_throughput = 11980.4 ops/s, KV hitrate = 71%. Diff vs baseline: -0.2% (within noise).
tariq: confirmed — revert fixes it. I'll hold off merging kernel_autoselect change until we add a canary test for KV hitrate.
maya: thanks everyone — opening an internal follow-up to add normalization unit tests and a microbench harness to catch this during PR CI.
